{
  "working_thesis": "Hannah Arendt's interpretation of the natural and the artificial in The Human Condition transforms inter-war German cultural criticism by subordinating ecological concerns to a political philosophy centered on human plurality, arguing that modernity's core threat is not technological dominance or environmental pollution, but the re-naturalization of the human world through biological necessity.",

    {
      "section_id": "sec-001",

      ],
      "title": "Introduction and Intellectual Contexts",
      "function": "front_matter",
      "key_concepts": [
        "de-naturalization",
        "re-naturalization",
        "world-alienation",
        "cultural criticism",
        "political philosophy"
      ],
      "depends_on_section_ids": [],
      "required_for_global_understanding": true,
      "unresolved_context": []
    },
    {

      ],

    },

      ],

    }
  ],
  "warnings": []
